title: Aldehyde vs Ketone: Why Aldehydes React Faster
subject: Chemistry
objective: Both have the same C=O, yet a nucleophile attacks an aldehyde faster. Two reasons: alkyl groups push electrons (+I) and lower the carbonyl carbon's δ+, and a ketone's two groups crowd the path to it. So HCHO > CH₃CHO > CH₃COCH₃.

fill.q: A nucleophile attacks the carbonyl ____ atom.
Alkyl groups release electrons; this is the +____ effect.
Blocking of the nucleophile by large groups is a ____ effect.
The most reactive carbonyl compound towards nucleophiles is ____.

tf.q: A ketone has two alkyl groups on its carbonyl carbon.
Alkyl groups make the carbonyl carbon more positive.
tf.explain: They release electrons and lower the δ+.

tf.q: Acetaldehyde is more reactive than acetone towards HCN.

ar.a: Ketones are less reactive than aldehydes.
ar.r: Two alkyl groups lower the δ+ and crowd the carbonyl carbon.

ar.a: Methanal is the most reactive aldehyde.
ar.r: It has two H and no alkyl group on the carbonyl carbon.

mcq.explain: Two H on the carbonyl carbon.

num.q: How many alkyl groups are on the carbonyl carbon of propanone?

short.q: Why is benzaldehyde less reactive than ethanal in nucleophilic addition?
short.solution: The benzene ring's resonance with the C=O lowers the carbonyl carbon's δ+.
